statement: Notice that 1 = 1 x 1, 1 + 3 = 2 x 2, 1 + 3 + 5 = 3 x 3 and 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 4 x 4. Using this pattern, what is 21 + 23 + 25 + ... + 39, the sum of all the odd numbers from 21 to 39?

choices.misconception: I used the pattern for the odd numbers up to 39 but forgot to take away 1 + 3 + ... + 19.
I counted 10 odd numbers from 21 to 39 and squared 10.
I thought 39 was the 19th odd number, so I worked out 19 x 19 - 10 x 10.
I took away the odd numbers up to 21 instead of up to 19, working out 20 x 20 - 11 x 11.

hints: Say the pattern in words: the sum of the first n odd numbers is what?
The sum of the first n odd numbers is n x n. Write your sum as all the odd numbers up to 39 minus all the odd numbers up to 19.
39 is the 20th odd number and 19 is the 10th. So the sum is 20 x 20 - 10 x 10.

solutions.reliable: The pattern says the sum of the first n odd numbers is n x n. The odd numbers up to 39 are the first 20 odd numbers, since 39 = 2 x 20 - 1, so they add up to 400. The odd numbers up to 19 are the first 10, adding up to 100. So 21 + 23 + ... + 39 = 400 - 100 = 300. Check: there are 10 numbers with average (21 + 39) / 2 = 30, and 10 x 30 = 300. The transferable idea: state the rule in general, then use it twice and subtract.
solutions.elegant: Ten odd numbers centred on 30 add up to 10 x 30 = 300, because they pair off as 21 + 39, 23 + 37, and so on, each pair making 60.

whyOnTest: Inferring a rule from examples: putting the pattern into words, then applying it to a sum that does not start at 1.
